title: Grothendieck existence for coherent systems with proper support on a separated finite-type scheme

standard_prerequisites.reference: Stable Stacks tags retained in assembly.external_references
standard_prerequisites.use: Coherent formal systems, Artin–Rees and formal functions, proper coherent pushforward, Chow lemma, Noetherian induction and support under proper maps. Projective/proper existence and the local push-pull/error and support lemmas are retained author proof, not given away as the target theorem.

core_obligations: Use Chow modification and projective algebraization to construct a candidate whose support cannot escape into the compactification boundary, by properness and the Jacobson property of the defining ideal.
Carry out Noetherian induction on annihilator ideals and use the retained push-pull error control and Serre-subcategory argument to obtain one proper closed support for the entire formal system.

proof_roadmap.step: Use Chow modification and projective algebraization to construct a candidate whose support cannot escape into the compactification boundary, by properness and the Jacobson property of the defining ideal.
Carry out Noetherian induction on annihilator ideals and use the retained push-pull error control and Serre-subcategory argument to obtain one proper closed support for the entire formal system.

difficulty_reason: Public projective formal existence does not establish proper support for a system on a nonproper ambient scheme. The compactification-boundary argument and induction through controlled kernel/cokernel errors supply independent H2 obligations; support in one common proper closed subscheme is the counted conclusion.

compared.difference: This migrates the existing unpublished research record, not an additional count beside it.
